projects.name: cinderx (Meta Cinder JIT for CPython)
projects.lead: Cinder JIT moved here (MIT, about 282 stars); find its own numbers vs stock CPython (pyperformance, Instagram figures); the old facebookincubator/cinder README claims are the fallback.

projects.name: lumen (Rust JavaScript engine)
projects.lead: Scores 3953 on macOS in ahaoboy's v8-v7 CI table (ahaoboy/js-engine-benchmark or similar); check repo docs for its own V8 or QuickJS comparison.

projects.name: CRuby RTL + MJIT (vnmakarov/ruby rtl_mjit_branch)
projects.lead: Branch rtl_mjit_branch README claims 6.18x geomean over Ruby 2.0 with GCC MJIT, optcarrot 2.7x; read the branch README tables (raw.githubusercontent.com/vnmakarov/ruby/rtl_mjit_branch/README.md); vnmakarov/mir is already catalogued, do not duplicate it.

projects.name: Topaz (Ruby on RPython)
projects.lead: Beats CRuby 2.7 in kostya/jit-benchmarks tables; find Topaz's own numbers and the kostya rows; state which Topaz fork (kostya) was measured.

projects.name: Quirrel (Squirrel fork)
projects.lead: Appears in daScript's dasProfile comparison table; check Quirrel's own docs/benchmarks and the daScript profile table for Lua columns.

projects.name: Porffor (AOT JavaScript/TypeScript to Wasm and native)
projects.lead: Find any committed benchmark comparing against Node/V8 or other engines; README states it is pre-alpha; record tier D if only claims.

projects.name: scriptc (Vercel Labs TypeScript to native compiler)
projects.lead: Look for benchmark tables vs Node in README or bench/ directory.

projects.name: BEAM.com (Erlang/OTP + Elixir single Cosmopolitan binary)
projects.lead: docs/BENCHMARKS.md has startup and fib numbers vs the stock BEAM; a modified runtime packaging, record what is actually faster.

projects.name: TinyKVM (Varnish KVM sandbox)
projects.lead: Same author as libriscv; look for docs comparing per-request or sandbox call overhead against Wasm runtimes or native; confirm the repo path first (varnish/tinykvm).

projects.name: ncruces/wasm2go (Wasm to Go compiler)
projects.lead: Separate project from goccy/wasm2go (already catalogued). Numbers vs wazero on a Core Ultra 7 258V in ncruces/go-sqlite3 discussion #361; read that discussion and any bench in the repo.

projects.name: FEX (x86/x86-64 emulator for ARM64 with JIT)
projects.lead: Box64 and rv8 are catalogued with QEMU baselines; find FEX's own numbers vs QEMU or Box64 (docs, wiki, blog posts linked from the repo).

projects.name: dstogov/ir (IR framework and JIT behind PHP 8.4+ JIT)
projects.lead: README claims generated code about 5% slower than gcc -O2 while compiling about 40x faster; look for the benchmark tables or scripts behind that claim.

projects.name: TurboPython / tpy (typed Python to C++ without GC)
projects.lead: Named in the Shed Skin README; its benchmark claims are unchecked, read the repo bench directory.

projects.name: EOS VM Optimized Compiler (AntelopeIO/spring eosvmoc)
projects.lead: EOS VM (AntelopeIO/eos-vm) is already catalogued; document the LLVM-based OC tier only if spring carries its own numbers vs eos-vm JIT or interpreter; else tier D.

projects.name: risechain/pevm (parallel EVM on revm)
projects.lead: README claims 2x average over sequential revm on Ethereum blocks and 22x on a Gigagas Uniswap block; numbers in crates/pevm/benches/README.md. revm itself is already catalogued.

projects.name: revmc (revm AOT/JIT compiler)
projects.lead: README chart is an image only; look for a benches/ directory or CI output with numbers vs revm interpreter and evmone.

projects.name: rsjsonnet (Rust jsonnet)
projects.lead: jrsonnet's docs/benchmarks.adoc shows rsjsonnet beating go-jsonnet everywhere (kube-prometheus 57.9 vs 1068.4 ms); jrsonnet is already a wave 12 record, so cite that table plus any rsjsonnet own numbers.

projects.name: Gambit Scheme
projects.lead: ecraven/r7rs-benchmarks all.csv (raw.githubusercontent.com/ecraven/r7rs-benchmarks/master/all.csv) gives gambit about 1.95x faster than Guile 3.0.11 geomean over 53 shared benchmarks (derived); label derived ratios; Guile is already catalogued.

projects.name: Bigloo Scheme
projects.lead: ecraven/r7rs-benchmarks all.csv: about 1.6x faster than Guile 3.0.11 geomean (derived); check the repo for its own benchmark page.

projects.name: Loko Scheme
projects.lead: gitlab.com is reachable here; ecraven/r7rs-benchmarks all.csv: about 1.6x faster than Guile 3.0.11 (derived); check its docs for own numbers.

projects.name: TypeScriptCompiler (ASDAlexander77, LLVM-based TypeScript AOT)
projects.lead: Look for README benchmark tables vs Node; record tier D if only claims.

projects.name: riscv-sbt (OpenISA RISC-V static binary translator)
projects.lead: Snippet claims MiBench slowdown 1.12x against rv8 3.16x and QEMU 7.07x; find the paper or results in the repo; rv8 is already catalogued.

projects.name: AngelScript JIT Compiler (BlindMindStudios)
projects.lead: r-lyeh/scriptorium table has 1.859 s for AngelScript JIT vs AngelScript 2.31.0 interpreter; AngelScript itself is catalogued; record the JIT's own ratio and the scriptorium harness caveats (bare lua from PATH, overhead=0, output unchecked).

projects.name: atJIT (autotuning JIT on Easy::jit)
projects.lead: Easy::jit is catalogued; find atJIT's own numbers (thesis or README) vs static compilation.

projects.name: expr-cls (Go expression evaluator from typed closures)
projects.lead: README claims 9.015 ns/op vs expr 172.0 and cel-go 267.9 ns/op on X+(6.0*Y), Ryzen 5 5600H, 3 stars; check that the benchmark code is committed and what it times.

projects.name: AssemblyScript (TypeScript-like to Wasm compiler)
projects.lead: Named in Perry's benchmarks/README.md as a peer; find its own published comparisons vs JS on V8 (the-assemblyscript-book or examples/benchmarks) and label derived ratios.

projects.name: zig-evm (cryptuon)
projects.lead: WebSearch claim of 5-6x parallel transaction execution, unverified; record tier D if there are no committed numbers; also note 0xjojoex/evm.zig in caveats if it has numbers.

projects.name: HashLink (Haxe virtual machine, Neko successor)
projects.lead: README has no numbers; look for Haxe benchmark pages linked from the repo (haxe.org benchmarks); tier D if only claims. NekoVM is catalogued.
